text:
Predicates:
Costs(x, y) ::: x costs y dollars.
CheaperThan(x, y) ::: x is cheaper than y.
ProvidesAid(x, y) ::: x provides financial aid to y.
ProveHardship(x) ::: x proves economic hardship.
LivesInSingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
HasFewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available.
ApplyingToTake(x, y) ::: x is applying to take y.
Premises:
Costs(graduateRecordExam, 205) ∧ CheaperThan(205, 300) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test, which is cheaper than $300.
ProvidesAid(ETS, y) → ProveHardship(y) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
LivesInSingleParentFamily(Tom) ∧ HasFewResources(Tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family and has few resources.
ApplyingToTake(Tom, GRE) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.
Conclusion:
Costs(graduateRecordExam, 205) ∧ CheaperThan(205, 300)
